newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-Santos buys East Spar stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-Santos buys East Spar stake.

text.p: Santos Ltd boosted its offshore interests on Wednesday, using pre-emptive purchase rights to buy WMC Ltd's 30 percent stake in the East Spar oil and condensate field off Western Australia.

The A$181 million acquisition, which cut out disappointed preferred bidder Novus Petroleum Ltd, will lift Santos' stake in the field to 45 percent and increase its interest in two other exploration permits in the Carnarvon Basin.
Santos announced a 1-for-8 rights issue at A$4.00 a share to raise A$270 million to fund the purchase, part of its planned A$800 million expansion plans for calendar 1997.
Managing director Ross Adler described the move as "a further important step in the development of Santos' Offshore Australia Business Unit".

WMC's interest in East Spar had been assessed as having proven and probable reserves of 160 petajoules of gas and 8.5 million barrels of condensate, and possible reserves of a further 9.6 million barrels of oil equivalent, Santos said.
The purchase was expected to enhance its earnings in 1997, but the expansion of capital would have a modestly dilutive impact on earnings per share in 1997.
The moves could dilute earnings per share by about five percent in 1997, analysts said, and Santos closed down 14 cents at A$4.75 after slipping up to 21 cents.
Analysts contacted by Reuters mainly saw the the purchase as good long-term strategic move, but were less enthusiastic about the equity raising.
One analyst, who declined to be named, said it was difficult to understand why Santos was issuing new shares at such a large discount.
He also said the company appeared to have paid "top dollar" as Novus had loaded its bid for the East Spar component of WMC's petroleum assets in an effort to avoid pre-emption.
Novus's A$183 million bid for the assets valued East Spar at A$173 million.
"They have paid a premium and they have paid it in the most expensive way through equity," the analyst said.
However, another analyst said it was the first capital raising by Santos for some time, and the share price should see only a small decline.
"I think they may escape relatively unscathed," he said.
Novus, which had hoped to gain synergies between East Spar and its Harriet field, said it was disappointed to have missed out on the purchase.
"I can't say we are surprised, but we are disappointed," said Novus general manager Bob Williams. "We would have liked to have captured East Spar."
However, he said he was satisfied that the junior oil and gas producer had acquired seven additional licence areas in the Carnarvon Basin, the remainder of WMC's assets, for A$6 million.
Williams said Novus had quadrupled its net acreage in the Carnarvon Basin, and also acquired WMC's substantial library and data base for a number of the areas.
Novus would finance the acquisition of WMC's interests in WA-215-P, TL/2, TP/7, WA-149-P and WA-263-P, from working capital and existing finance.

Novus noted that in WA-263-P, adjacent to the North West Shelf LNG gas fields, Woodside and Mobil had farmed into the block and would carry Novus' newly acquired interest through the current work programme. A well was likely to be drilled in 1998.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
